data.description:
## Description
**What**: Add a sentry on the ticket-transition hook so that a status transition closed->open on a bug carrying the negative-example tag automatically removes that tag. A reopened bug is consequently excluded from negative-examples-lookup.sh results.
**Why**: Prevents stale lessons from reopened (no-longer-resolved) bugs leaking into test-writer guidance.
**Scope**:
- IN: ticket-transition hook sentry for closed->open on negative-example-tagged bugs; tag removal; consequent lookup exclusion.
- OUT: the lookup script itself (draft-3); the twelve-scenario synthetic test (draft-8, which includes the reopening fixture).

## Done Definitions

- A status transition from closed to open on a bug carrying the negative-example tag removes the negative-example tag via the ticket-transition hook sentry ← Satisfies: sc-8
- After such a reopening the bug is excluded from negative-examples-lookup.sh results ← Satisfies: sc-8
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic ← Satisfies: sc-8

## Considerations

- [Risk] The sentry must fire only on closed->open (not on other transitions) and only when the negative-example tag is present, to avoid removing tags on unrelated transitions.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, I want reopening a tagged bug to automatically remove its negative-example tag, so that reopened bugs are excluded from lookup until re-extraction.
